Create a Local Source

Source: R/local-source.R
og_local.Rd

A Local Source answers queries from Store Releases downloaded to this machine, through ogquery, the Store Reader. Give it the directory of each GWAS Store, one element per GWAS Store. A GWAS Store directory holds one Store Release, one level down: the directory there holding a manifest.json. It is searched one level down and never deeper, so the Dense Component inside a Hybrid Store Release (<release>/dense/manifest.json) is never taken for a Store Release, and hidden directories (whose names start with .), such as a build in progress, are skipped. A Store Release's own directory (the one holding its manifest.json) works too. One that has lost its manifest.json (it still holds data.zarr or analyses.tsv) is refused, never searched as a GWAS Store directory. Each Store Release names itself by its manifest (store_id, release_id, format_version), and a Local Source holds at most one Store Release of each GWAS Store, so no query ever chooses between Store Releases.

Usage

og_local(
  gwas = NULL,
  plink = NULL,
  bfile = NULL,
  ld_store = NULL,
  geno_store = NULL,
  inherit = NULL
)

Arguments

gwas

The directory of each GWAS Store, or of each Store Release: a character vector, one element per GWAS Store. NULL (the default) for none: an LD-only Local Source, which needs bfile. A Local Source with neither Store Releases nor an LD resource is refused (class opengwasr_argument).

plink

The PLINK 1.9 or 2 binary, for bfile: its path, or a command on your PATH, such as "plink2" (as in a shell, a name without a path separator is a command). NULL takes the first supported PLINK of the genetics.binaRies package, if it is installed, then plink, then plink2, on your PATH, skipping any that isn't supported; if there is none, it stops (class opengwasr_plink_not_found, with skipped: plink_bin and version of each one skipped) and says how to install it.

bfile

A PLINK binary fileset's prefix (without .bed, .bim or .fam): the Source's LD resource, a PLINK Reference. LD from a PLINK Reference is computed from its genotypes without adjusting for population structure (principal components), unlike OpenGWAS LD Stores and Genotype Stores, so it may be less accurate. opengwasr warns of this once per PLINK Reference in a session (class opengwasr_plink_unadjusted).

ld_store

A downloaded LD Store. Not available yet.

geno_store

A downloaded Genotype Store. Not available yet.

inherit

A Local Source to build this one like, as described under "Inheriting".

Value

An og_local_source. Its releases is a data frame with one row per Store Release: store_id, release_id, format_version and path (the Store Release's own directory), with no rows for an LD-only Local Source. Its LD resource is read with og_ld_resource(): an og_plink_reference, or NULL.

Details

og_local() reads no Associations. It checks that each path is, or holds, a Store Release that the installed ogquery can read, and refuses the Source otherwise:

  • a path that doesn't exist, or holds no Store Release (no manifest in it or one level down, or one ogquery can't parse): opengwasr_not_store_release, with e$paths and why each was refused, e$reasons;

  • a GWAS Store directory holding several Store Releases: opengwasr_several_releases, with one element per Store Release found in e$directory (the GWAS Store directory given), e$store_id, e$release_id, e$releases (<store_id>/<release_id>) and e$paths, so you can give the one you want;

  • a Store Release whose format version ogquery can't read: opengwasr_format_unsupported, with e$paths, each one's version (e$format_version) and the format series ogquery reads (e$readable);

  • two Store Releases of one GWAS Store: opengwasr_duplicate_store.

Python

The first local call finds Python and ogquery. A Python you chose always wins, in the order reticulate ranks them: RETICULATE_PYTHON (a Python, or its directory), RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV, an environment you selected with reticulate::use_virtualenv(), reticulate::use_condaenv() or reticulate::use_python(), or an activated virtualenv (VIRTUAL_ENV); or a Python reticulate has already started in this session. If it lacks ogquery, the error says how to install it there. opengwasr never swaps it for another: if reticulate can't start the Python you chose and starts a lower choice, its automatic one or one it found itself instead, og_local() refuses. Otherwise (and with RETICULATE_PYTHON=managed or RETICULATE_USE_MANAGED_VENV=true, which ask for it) reticulate sets one up automatically with uv (reticulate::py_require("ogquery>=0.1.0,<1")), which needs the internet the first time.

opengwasr reads ogquery >=0.1.0,<1. An ogquery outside that range, or without ogquery.release (such as the placeholder 0.0.0 on PyPI), is refused before anything is read.

One gap: a use_virtualenv(), use_condaenv() or use_python() call can't be seen before Python starts, so opengwasr declares ogquery with py_require() as for no choice. Once Python has started, reticulate's py_config() names the call (forced), and opengwasr reports it (chosen_by = "use_python"). But if reticulate can't start that environment and starts its automatic one, py_config() names only the automatic one, and opengwasr can't tell. Set RETICULATE_PYTHON to close the gap.

Without reticulate, og_local() offers to install it, or, when R isn't interactive, stops with opengwasr_local_unavailable, as it does whenever no Python with ogquery can be found. That error carries e$need ("reticulate", "python", "ogquery", "ogquery_version" or "chosen_python"), e$found (for "ogquery_version", the ogquery version found, or NA for none), e$required (the ogquery versions opengwasr supports, ">=0.1.0,<1"), e$python, e$chosen_by (how the Python was chosen: "RETICULATE_PYTHON", "RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV", "use_python", "VIRTUAL_ENV", "automatic" or "reticulate", one reticulate found itself), e$started_by (for "chosen_python", how the Python reticulate started instead was chosen), e$install (the command that installs what is missing, when there is one; for an unsupported ogquery in reticulate's automatic Python, the command that clears uv's cached ogquery, after which restarting R sets up a supported one) and e$setting (the setting that names a Python). og_local_check() reports what was found.

LD resource

A Local Source carries the LD resource that answers LD for it (ADR 0006; see vignette("local-source"), "Clumping and LD"), and the LD is chosen there and nowhere else. Today that is a PLINK Reference: bfile names a PLINK binary fileset (.bed, .bim, .fam) on your machine, and plink the PLINK binary that reads it. og_local() checks the fileset (class opengwasr_plink_reference_missing, with e$files) and finds PLINK. og_tophits() then clumps on the fly with it (r2 and kb are required: a PLINK Reference has no recorded defaults, class opengwasr_plink_settings_required), and og_clump() and og_ld_matrix() read it. Without an LD resource, anything that needs LD is refused (class opengwasr_ld_resource_required), naming the LD resources in e$forms ("bfile" and "api_two_step": the API's LD Stores, by clumping on an API Source you name, og_clump(og_api(), og_tophits(src, ids, clump = FALSE))) and, when clumping, clump = FALSE (e$clump_false): a Local Source never calls the API itself.

Variants are matched to a PLINK Reference by rsID, because PLINK References are usually on GRCh37 while ALIDs are on GRCh38: from a data frame's rsid column, else looked up in the Source's Store Releases. A variant with no rsID, or whose rsID isn't in the .bim, is left out, and a message (class opengwasr_plink_unmatched, with count) says how many. PLINK 1.9 and PLINK 2 (2.0.0-a.6.0 or later) both work, and give the same answer: each is asked for the same thing in its own words (an LD matrix of r with the reference's allele order kept: --r square --keep-allele-order in 1.9, --r-unphased square ref-based in 2; clumping with --clump, read from .clumped or .clumps). Its version is read once, here (--version), and kept on the PLINK Reference (og_ld_resource()) and in the provenance of what it computes (plink_version, beside plink_bin). A plink that is any other PLINK, such as 1.07 or an earlier PLINK 2, or a program that isn't PLINK, is refused (class opengwasr_plink_unsupported, with version, the version found or NA, supported, and suggest, a supported "plink" or "plink2" on your PATH, or NULL).

An LD-only Local Source. og_local(bfile = ) with no gwas holds no Store Releases and needs no Python. It answers og_clump() and og_ld_matrix() for data you already have, such as top hits from the API Source, when PLINK can match the variants by rsID: a data frame with an rsid column, or rsIDs. ALIDs would need a GWAS Store to look up their rsIDs, so they are refused (class opengwasr_gwas_store_required, with the ALIDs in e$alids), naming the ways round in e$forms: "gwas" (og_local(gwas = , bfile = )), "rsid_column" (a data frame with an rsid column) and "api_rsids" (their rsIDs looked up first with og_variants_chrpos(og_api(), positions)). Every verb that reads Associations or Analyses refuses it with the same class, and e$forms "gwas".

ld_store (a downloaded LD Store) and geno_store (a Genotype Store) are refused until opengwasr can read them (classes opengwasr_ld_resource_unavailable and opengwasr_local_unsupported, with e$resource). Giving more than one kind of LD resource is refused (class opengwasr_ld_resource_mixed, with e$given), and so is plink without bfile. An error about bfile or plink names it in e$arg.

Inheriting

og_local(inherit = src, ...) builds a Local Source like src: every argument given replaces the inherited one, and the rest come from src. Without gwas, its Store Releases are src's, not opened again. Giving any of plink, bfile, ld_store and geno_store replaces src's LD resource whole, never mixed with it: og_local(inherit = src, bfile = ref) gives src's Store Releases a PLINK Reference, and og_local(inherit = src, bfile = NULL) drops it. The one exception is plink alone: og_local(inherit = src, plink = "plink2") keeps src's PLINK Reference's fileset and changes the PLINK that reads it (plink = NULL finds one again). og_local(inherit = src, gwas = NULL) drops the Store Releases and keeps the LD resource: an LD-only Local Source. What is given is checked as for any other Local Source. Anything but a Local Source as inherit is refused (class opengwasr_argument).

See also

og_local_check(), og_api().

Examples

stores <- system.file("stores", package = "opengwasr")
# GWAS Store directories, and, for hyb, which holds two, a Store Release directory
src <- og_local(c(file.path(stores, c("dense", "ragged")), file.path(stores, "hyb", "v1")))
src
#> <og_local_source>
#> • Store Releases: 3
#> • s/r: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/stores/dense/r
#> • residual-rag/comp: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/stores/ragged/comp
#> • hyb/v1: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/stores/hyb/v1
#> • LD resource: none
# With a PLINK Reference as its LD resource, where PLINK is installed:
bfile <- file.path(system.file("plink", package = "opengwasr"), "ref")
ld_only <- tryCatch(og_local(bfile = bfile), error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(ld_only)) {
  og_ld_matrix(ld_only, c("rs5000", "rs1000"))
  src <- og_local(inherit = src, bfile = bfile)
  og_tophits(src, "s:bmi_irn", r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)
}
